article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 75% Indica / 25% Sativa
Genetics: White Widow × AK-47
Breeder: Dinafem Seeds
THC Content: 22%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, sour citrus, earth, resin
Flowering Time (Indoor): 50–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: 550 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 1,200 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

White Siberian is a meeting of two marijuana strains that helped define the 1990s: the frost-covered White Widow and the famously potent AK-47. Dinafem combined an elite White Widow clone with AK-47 to build a faster, stronger, more productive indica-dominant plant without losing the resin that made the White family famous. Mature flowers become thick and compact, secondary branches fill with numerous smaller buds, and the entire plant can develop a heavy trichome coating that immediately explains why the cultivar has remained attractive to hash makers as well as flower growers.

What separates this hybrid from a simple nostalgia project is its practical garden performance. Indoor plants can finish in as little as 50–65 days while producing around 550 g/m², and outdoor specimens have the potential to reach roughly 2.5 meters and yield as much as 1,200 grams each. At approximately 22% THC, the strain also carries enough strength to satisfy experienced consumers. Sweet fruit and sour notes soften the earthy indica foundation, while the high moves through both mind and body before settling into prolonged relaxation.
Genetics and Lineage

Dinafem bred White Siberian from an elite White Widow clone crossed with AK-47. White Widow brings one of the most recognizable genetic traditions in modern cannabis. Dinafem’s White Widow line was maintained from an elite clone dating to the late 1990s and selected around vigorous growth, heavy resin, dense flowers, and pronounced relaxation. Its influence is especially visible late in bloom, when trichomes can accumulate so heavily that flowers appear pale or dusted in white.

AK-47 contributes a more globally mixed genetic background. Serious Seeds developed the famous line from Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan ancestry, creating a sativa-dominant hybrid that combined strong cerebral effects with relatively fast flowering, thick resinous buds, and a later physical component. That combination made AK-47 especially useful in breeding because it could introduce vigor and mental intensity without demanding the extremely long bloom associated with many tropical sativas.

The finished cross leans strongly toward the indica side at roughly 75%, yet AK-47 prevents it from becoming flat or completely narcotic. White Widow establishes the dense structure, resin, and physical heaviness, while AK-47 adds energy, branching, psychoactive intensity, and a slightly brighter dimension to the experience. The pairing also helps explain White Siberian’s unusually short bloom and substantial production: both parental lines were already prized for delivering strong flower without an excessive cultivation cycle.
Effects and Experience

White Siberian begins with enough mental activity to feel more balanced than its indica percentage suggests. The early stage can bring a noticeable change in mood, increased interest in conversation or music, and a clear sense of psychoactive intensity. It is not typically a sharp, racing sativa experience; instead, the mental component feels broad and substantial, with AK-47 influence lifting the head while White Widow keeps the experience grounded.

Physical relaxation becomes increasingly dominant as the session develops. Muscles loosen, movement feels less urgent, and the initial cerebral activity gradually gives way to a longer-lasting body calm. At moderate servings, the strain can feel comfortably balanced, but higher doses are more likely to encourage stillness, appetite, and eventual drowsiness. Dinafem specifically described the effect as powerful, relaxing, and long lasting, which fits its 75% indica composition well.

With breeder-listed THC around 22%, this is not mild cannabis. People with limited tolerance may experience dizziness, dry mouth, dry eyes, mental fog, or temporary anxiety if they consume too much too quickly. Experienced users may find the potency more manageable, especially because the strong body component tends to settle the experience over time. Smaller servings preserve more of the mental lift, while larger amounts bring the heavier indica personality decisively to the front.
Medical Benefits

The deep physical component may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer marijuana with substantial relaxation rather than prolonged stimulation. As the strain develops, muscular tightness and general physical discomfort may feel less intrusive, while the calmer mental state can make it easier to disengage from stress after a demanding day. The combination is generally better suited to evening use than situations requiring high levels of concentration or coordination.

Appetite stimulation is another commonly associated characteristic, and stronger servings can become noticeably sedating. That later-stage heaviness may appeal to consumers looking for a cultivar that fits a nighttime routine, although high THC should still be approached cautiously. People sensitive to intoxicating cannabis may find that a large dose produces more mental impairment or anxiety than relaxation, particularly during the earlier psychoactive phase.

Dinafem laboratory samples averaged about 2.342% total terpenes, indicating an aromatic flower with a relatively substantial volatile profile. The breeder did not publish a universal dominant-terpene ranking for every plant, so medical effects should not be attributed to one assumed compound. Batch-specific cannabinoid and terpene testing, individual tolerance, medications, and previous response to THC-rich cannabis are more useful guides than the strain name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness is the first major aromatic theme. The flower can give off a rich fruit character that feels fuller than simple citrus, followed by a slightly sour edge that prevents the bouquet from becoming overly soft. That contrast gives White Siberian a recognizable old-school personality: sweet, resinous, pungent, and earthy rather than creamy or candy-like in the modern dessert sense.

The deeper layers come from the indica side of the pedigree. Earth, plant resin, and mild spice become more obvious once the buds are broken apart, while a sour note adds brightness around the edges. Certain plants may lean fruitier, whereas others emphasize the earthy White Widow foundation. The aroma can become surprisingly strong during late flowering, particularly because the dense resin production concentrates the plant’s volatile compounds.

On the palate, sweet fruit generally arrives first before sour and earthy characteristics emerge through the exhale. Vaporization can preserve the fruit and lighter aromatic details, while combustion tends to emphasize resin and the heavier traditional indica character. A careful dry and cure are important because rushed processing can mute the sweeter side and leave behind a much flatter earthy profile.
Growing Information

White Siberian is one of Dinafem’s more beginner-friendly high-potency cultivars. Plants grow vigorously with a strong central stem, sturdy secondary branches, and a Christmas-tree-like structure that naturally supports numerous flowering sites. Rooting is strong, vegetative growth is reliable, and the plant generally does not require complicated training to produce a respectable canopy. Indoors, topping or light low-stress training can still improve horizontal coverage when growers want to maximize light distribution.

Flowering takes approximately 50–65 days, with indoor production around 550 g/m² under strong conditions. Mature buds become large, compact, and exceptionally resinous, and branches may require support as weight accumulates. The cultivar performs well in indoor gardens and greenhouses, but odor control and late-flower humidity management are important. Dense flowers can become vulnerable to mold when exposed to persistently damp conditions, so good airflow is more valuable than excessive defoliation.

Outdoors, White Siberian can reach approximately 2.5 meters and produce up to 1,200 grams per plant in favorable environments. Dinafem favored dry, sunny, temperate conditions, where the plant can fully exploit its vigor and branching. Harvest generally arrives in early to mid-October. Although the genetics are sturdy and resilient, prolonged wet weather near maturity should still be taken seriously because the same compact flower structure responsible for impressive yields can retain moisture if the canopy remains damp.
FAQ
What strains make White Siberian?

White Siberian was bred by Dinafem Seeds from an elite White Widow clone crossed with AK-47. White Widow contributes dense resinous flowers and strong indica effects, while AK-47 adds vigor, psychoactive intensity, and a more cerebral component.
Is White Siberian indica or sativa?

White Siberian is approximately 75% indica and 25% sativa. Its compact flowers, heavy resin, and relaxing body effects clearly favor the indica side, although AK-47 gives the high a noticeable cerebral dimension.
How much THC does White Siberian have?

Dinafem lists White Siberian at approximately 22% THC with low CBD. Actual potency can vary according to phenotype, cultivation method, lighting, environment, harvest maturity, and laboratory testing.
What does White Siberian taste like?

The flavor combines sweet fruit with sour notes, earth, resin, and mild spice. It has a traditional pungent indica profile rather than the creamy candy or dessert flavors common in many newer hybrids.
How long does White Siberian take to flower?
Indoor flowering generally takes approximately 50–65 days. Outdoor plants typically reach maturity from early to mid-October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on White Siberian

White Siberian brings together two strains whose reputations were already firmly established before modern cannabis breeding became dominated by dessert names and extreme THC marketing. White Widow contributes its famous frost, dense flower structure, and relaxing character, while AK-47 introduces vigor, global sativa influence, and a stronger cerebral dimension. The combination produces a cultivar that feels recognizably old-school without sacrificing production or potency.

Its cultivation numbers remain impressive. Around 550 g/m² indoors, outdoor harvests potentially reaching 1,200 grams per plant, a 50–65-day flowering period, and strong vegetative performance give growers substantial production without an unusually complicated routine. The main concern is moisture late in bloom, when dense resinous flowers need steady airflow and protection from persistently wet conditions.

For consumers, the strain delivers sweet and sour fruit over an earthy resinous base, followed by effects that move from a noticeable mental lift toward sustained body relaxation. At roughly 22% THC, it retains enough strength to compete with much newer weed while preserving the flavor and physical character associated with classic 1990s genetics. White Siberian remains one of Dinafem’s clearest examples of using two established cannabis legends to create a hybrid that is practical, potent, resinous, and unmistakably traditional.
